actions.title: Zip
actions.description: Pack the selected items into one zip file.
explain: zip — the program that makes zip files
-r — include everything inside folders
{{out:Archive.zip}} — the new file; an existing file is never overwritten
the selected items — what goes in it

variants.title: Smallest file
variants.description: Spend more time to make the zip as small as possible.
explain: zip -r -9 — pack folders too, at the best compression
{{out:Archive.zip}} — the new file; never overwrites
the selected items — what goes in it

variants.title: No hidden files
variants.description: Leave out hidden files such as .DS_Store and .git.
explain: zip -r — pack folders too
-x '*.DS_Store' -x '*/.*' -x '.*' — skip Finder clutter and any hidden file or folder
{{out:Archive.zip}} — the new file; never overwrites

actions.title: Unzip
actions.description: Unpack a zip file into a new folder next to it.
explain: unzip — the program that opens zip files
-d — put the contents in this folder
{{out:<stem>}} — a new folder named after the zip

variants.title: Into this folder
variants.description: Unpack next to the zip without overwriting anything.
explain: unzip -n — unpack here, and never replace a file that already exists

variants.title: List contents only
variants.description: Show what's inside without unpacking.
explain: unzip -l — list the files and their sizes; nothing is unpacked

actions.title: Make tar.gz
actions.description: Pack the selected items into a compressed tar archive.
explain: tar -czf — create a compressed archive file
{{out:Archive.tar.gz}} — the new file; never overwrites
the selected items — what goes in it

variants.title: Without Mac metadata
variants.description: Skip the hidden ._ files macOS adds, for archives that will be opened on Linux.
explain: COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 — don't add macOS's extra ._ files
tar -czf — create a compressed archive file
{{out:Archive.tar.gz}} — the new file; never overwrites

actions.title: Make tar.zst
actions.description: Pack the selected items into a zstd-compressed tar archive: fast, and usually smaller than gzip.
explain: COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 — don't add macOS's extra ._ files
tar -cf - — bundle the items into one stream
zstd -T0 -3 — compress it using every CPU core, at the balanced level 3
-o {{out:Archive.tar.zst}} — the new file; never overwrites

variants.title: Fastest (level 1)
variants.description: Quickest, with a little less compression.
explain: zstd -T0 -1 — the fastest level, using every CPU core

variants.title: High (level 19)
variants.description: Much smaller than the default and still opens quickly; slow to make.
explain: zstd -T0 -19 — high compression, using every CPU core

variants.title: Maximum (level 22)
variants.description: The smallest zstd can make. Slow, and needs a lot of memory; opening needs more memory too.
explain: --ultra -22 — the highest compression level
--long=27 — look for repeats across a 128 MB window, which shrinks big archives further
-T0 — use every CPU core
Asks first because it can take a long time and a lot of memory

actions.title: Extract tar
actions.description: Unpack a tar archive here.
explain: tar -xf — extract the archive's files into this folder

actions.title: Extract tar.zst
actions.description: Unpack a zstd-compressed tar archive here.
explain: zstd -dc — decompress to a stream
--long=31 — allows archives made with the long-range setting
tar -xf - — unpack the stream into this folder

actions.title: Find by name
actions.description: List files in this folder and below whose name contains some text.
explain: find . — look in this folder and everything below it
-iname — match the name, ignoring capital letters
-not -path '*/.*' — skip hidden folders

variants.title: Files only
variants.description: Only match files, not folders.
explain: find . -type f — look at files only
-iname — match the name, ignoring capital letters
-not -path '*/.*' — skip hidden folders

variants.title: Folders only
variants.description: Only match folders.
explain: find . -type d — look at folders only
-iname — match the name, ignoring capital letters

variants.title: Exact capitals
variants.description: Match capital letters exactly.
explain: -name — match the name exactly, capitals included

actions.title: Search inside files
actions.description: List lines in files here and below that contain some text.
explain: grep — search for text
-r — go into folders
-I — skip binary files
-n — show line numbers

variants.title: Ignore capitals
variants.description: Match text whatever its capitals.
explain: -i — ignore capital letters
-r -I -n — go into folders, skip binary files, show line numbers

variants.title: Whole word
variants.description: Match whole words only, so 'cat' doesn't find 'catalog'.
explain: -w — the text must be a whole word
-r -I -n — go into folders, skip binary files, show line numbers

variants.title: File names only
variants.description: List which files contain it, without the lines.
explain: -l — show only the names of files that contain a match
-r -I — go into folders, skip binary files

actions.title: Largest files
actions.description: Show the 20 largest files in this folder and below.
explain: find . -type f — every file below here
du -k — its size in kilobytes
sort -rn | head -20 — biggest first, keep 20

variants.title: Top 50
variants.description: Show the 50 largest instead of 20.
explain: sort -rn | head -50 — biggest first, keep 50

actions.title: Folder sizes
actions.description: Show how big each item in this folder is.
explain: du -sh — total size, human-readable
sort -rh — biggest first

actions.title: Convert to PNG
actions.description: Make PNG copies of the selected images.
explain: sips — the macOS image tool
-s format png — save as PNG
--out — the new file; the original stays

actions.title: Convert to JPEG
actions.description: Make JPEG copies of the selected images. Set the quality: 100 is best, lower makes smaller files.
explain: sips -s format jpeg — save as JPEG
-s formatOptions — JPEG quality: 100 is best, 85 is a good balance, 60 is small
--out — the new file; the original stays

variants.title: Web (quality 75)
variants.description: Smaller files that still look fine on screen.
explain: -s formatOptions 75 — a good size for web pages and email

variants.title: Maximum quality (100)
variants.description: Least compression; the files are larger.
explain: -s formatOptions 100 — the highest JPEG quality

variants.title: Tiny (quality 40)
variants.description: Very small files with visible loss, for previews.
explain: -s formatOptions 40 — strong compression

actions.title: Resize image
actions.description: Make a smaller copy of an image. Pick a variant to fit a width or height, crop to an exact size, or scale by a percentage.
explain: sips -Z — shrink so the longest side is this many pixels; the shape is kept
--out — the new file; the original stays

variants.title: Fit to width
variants.description: Set the width in pixels; the height follows so nothing is squashed.
explain: --resampleWidth — make the picture this many pixels wide
the height follows to keep the shape

variants.title: Fit to height
variants.description: Set the height in pixels; the width follows so nothing is squashed.
explain: --resampleHeight — make the picture this many pixels tall
the width follows to keep the shape

variants.title: Exact size, cropped
variants.description: Fill an exact width and height, cutting off the overflow from the centre. Nothing is stretched.
variants.command: W={{ask:Width (pixels)=1200}}; H={{ask:Height (pixels)=800}}; O={{out:<stem> cropped.<ext>}}; cp {{file}} "$O" && set -- $(sips -g pixelWidth -g pixelHeight "$O" | awk '/pixel/{print $2}') && if [ $(( $1 * H )) -gt $(( $2 * W )) ]; then sips --resampleHeight $H "$O" >/dev/null; else sips --resampleWidth $W "$O" >/dev/null; fi && sips --cropToHeightWidth $H $W "$O"
explain: The picture is first scaled until it covers the whole box
Then --cropToHeightWidth trims the extra from the centre
Works on a copy, so the original is never touched

variants.title: 50% smaller
variants.description: Half the width and half the height.
variants.command: w=$(sips -g pixelWidth {{file}} | awk '/pixelWidth/{print $2}'); sips --resampleWidth $(( w / 2 )) {{file}} --out {{out:<stem> half.<ext>}}
explain: Reads the current width, then makes the copy half as wide
The height follows, so it is half the size both ways

variants.title: 25% smaller
variants.description: Three quarters of the width and height.
explain: Reads the current width, then makes the copy three quarters as wide
The height follows to keep the shape

variants.title: Custom percent
variants.description: Scale to any percentage of the original size.
variants.command: w=$(sips -g pixelWidth {{file}} | awk '/pixelWidth/{print $2}'); p={{ask:Percent of original=50}}; sips --resampleWidth $(( w * p / 100 )) {{file}} --out {{out:<stem> scaled.<ext>}}
explain: Reads the current width, then scales it by the percentage you give
50 means half the size, 200 means twice

variants.title: Resize and save as JPEG
variants.description: Shrink to a longest side and save as a JPEG with the quality you choose.
variants.command: sips -Z {{ask:Longest side (pixels)=1600}} -s format jpeg -s formatOptions {{ask:Quality (1-100)=80}} {{file}} --out {{out:<stem> small.jpg}}
explain: -Z — shrink so the longest side is this many pixels
-s format jpeg — save as JPEG
-s formatOptions — JPEG quality: 100 is best, lower makes smaller files

actions.title: PDF to text
actions.description: Extract the text of a PDF into a .txt file.
explain: pdftotext — reads the text out of a PDF

actions.title: Markdown to HTML
actions.description: Make an HTML page from a Markdown file.
explain: pandoc — converts between document formats
-o — the new file

actions.title: Video to MP4
actions.description: Make an MP4 copy of a video.
explain: ffmpeg -i — read this video
-c:v libx264 -c:a aac — the common MP4 picture and sound formats

variants.title: Smaller file
variants.description: Re-encode harder for a smaller file, with a little less quality.
explain: -crf 28 — lower quality than the default (23), noticeably smaller

variants.title: Fast, no re-encode
variants.description: Rewrap the same picture and sound in an MP4, which takes seconds. Only works if the formats fit MP4.
explain: -c copy — keep the picture and sound exactly as they are
only the container changes, so quality is untouched

actions.title: Extract audio
actions.description: Save the sound of a video as an MP3.
explain: -vn — drop the picture
-q:a 2 — good MP3 quality

actions.title: Video details
actions.description: Show duration, size and codecs of a video.
explain: ffprobe — reports what is inside a media file

actions.title: File hashes
actions.description: Show the MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 fingerprints of each selected file.
actions.command: for f in {{selection}}; do echo "$f"; echo "  MD5     $(md5 -q "$f")"; echo "  SHA-1   $(shasum -a 1 "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)"; echo "  SHA-256 $(shasum -a 256 "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)"; echo "  SHA-512 $(shasum -a 512 "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)"; echo; done
explain: for f in … — repeat for each selected item
md5 -q — the MD5 fingerprint, short and old; fine for spotting accidental changes
shasum -a 1 / 256 / 512 — the SHA family; SHA-256 is what most download pages list
cut -d' ' -f1 — keep just the hash, not the file name

variants.title: SHA-256 only
variants.description: Just the SHA-256, the one most download pages list.
explain: shasum -a 256 — a fingerprint of each file's contents

variants.title: SHA-512 only
variants.description: Just the SHA-512, the longest and strongest.
explain: shasum -a 512 — a longer fingerprint of each file's contents

variants.title: MD5 only
variants.description: Just the MD5, short and old; fine for spotting accidental changes.
explain: md5 — a short fingerprint; not safe against tampering

actions.title: Check a hash
actions.description: Compare a file with the SHA-256 or MD5 hash a download page gave you.
actions.command: h={{ask:Expected hash=}}; [ -n "$h" ] || { echo "Paste the hash you were given into the box above first."; exit 1; }; h=$(printf %s "$h" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -d ' '); case ${#h} in 64) a=$(shasum -a 256 {{file}} | cut -d' ' -f1);; 32) a=$(md5 -q {{file}});; 40) a=$(shasum -a 1 {{file}} | cut -d' ' -f1);; 128) a=$(shasum -a 512 {{file}} | cut -d' ' -f1);; *) echo "That doesn't look like an MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 or SHA-512 hash."; exit 1;; esac; if [ "$a" = "$h" ]; then echo "MATCH: the file is exactly what the hash describes."; echo "$a"; else echo "DIFFERENT: do not trust this file."; echo "expected $h"; echo "actual   $a"; exit 2; fi
explain: The hash you paste is lower-cased and spaces are removed
Its length decides which kind it is: 32 = MD5, 40 = SHA-1, 64 = SHA-256, 128 = SHA-512
The file's own hash of that kind is worked out and compared
MATCH means the file is unchanged; DIFFERENT means it was altered, damaged or isn't the file you think

actions.title: Count lines and words
actions.description: Count lines, words and bytes in the selected files.
explain: wc — counts lines, words and bytes

actions.title: What kind of file?
actions.description: Show what each selected file really contains.
explain: file — looks at the contents, not the name

actions.title: List with details
actions.description: List this folder with sizes, dates and permissions.
explain: ls -lah — long format, all files, readable sizes

variants.title: Newest first
variants.description: Sort by modified time, newest at the top.
explain: ls -laht — long format, all files, readable sizes, newest first

variants.title: Folders only
variants.description: List only the folders.
explain: ls -lahd */ — details for each folder, not what's inside

actions.title: Remove download warning
actions.description: Clear the 'downloaded from the internet' flag so macOS stops asking.
explain: xattr -d — delete an extended attribute
com.apple.quarantine — the download warning flag

actions.title: Status
actions.description: Show which files changed, which are staged, and the branch you're on.
explain: git status — what changed since the last commit
--short — one line per file; two letters show staged then unstaged
--branch — also shows the branch and how far it is from its remote

variants.title: Full
variants.description: The long form, with hints about what to do next.
explain: git status — the full report, with suggestions for each state

variants.title: Include ignored
variants.description: Also list files that .gitignore hides.
explain: --ignored — also show files that git is told to leave alone

actions.title: Log
actions.description: The latest commits, one per line.
explain: git log --oneline — one short line per commit
--decorate — show branch and tag names beside the commits it applies to
-20 — only the latest 20

variants.title: Graph, all branches
variants.description: Show how branches split and merge.
explain: --graph — draw the branch structure
--all — include every branch, not just this one
-30 — the latest 30

variants.title: With author and date
variants.description: Each commit with who made it and when.
explain: --pretty=format — choose the columns: short id, date, author, message
-30 — the latest 30

actions.title: Diff
actions.description: What changed in your files since the last commit, as a summary.
explain: git diff — compare your files with the last commit
--stat — a summary: each file and how many lines changed

variants.title: Full changes
variants.description: Every changed line.
explain: git diff — every added and removed line, not saved yet

variants.title: Staged only
variants.description: What will go into the next commit.
explain: --staged — compare what you've staged with the last commit

actions.title: Branches
actions.description: List branches, and which commit each one is on.
explain: git branch -vv — local branches with their latest commit and the remote branch they follow

variants.title: Include remote
variants.description: Also the branches on the remote.
explain: -a — include remote branches too

variants.title: Remotes
variants.description: Show where this repository fetches from and pushes to.
explain: git remote -v — the names and web addresses of the remotes

actions.title: File history
actions.description: Every commit that changed the selected file, following renames.
explain: git log --oneline — one short line per commit
--follow — keep going through renames
-- {{file}} — only commits that touched this file

variants.title: With the changes
variants.description: Show what changed in each commit, for this file.
explain: -p — include the actual lines changed in each commit

actions.title: Stage selected
actions.description: Add the selected files to the next commit.
explain: git add — put these files in the next commit
-- — what follows is file names, never options

actions.title: Unstage selected
actions.description: Take the selected files out of the next commit. Your edits stay.
explain: git reset — take them back out of the next commit
the files themselves are not changed

actions.title: Commit staged
actions.description: Save the staged files as a commit with your message.
actions.command: m={{ask:Commit message=}}; [ -n "$m" ] || { echo "Type a commit message in the box above first."; exit 1; }; git commit -m "$m"
explain: The message you type in the box becomes the commit message
git commit -m — save everything staged as a new commit
Nothing is sent anywhere; Push does that

actions.title: Pull
actions.description: Bring in the remote's new commits, only if that needs no merge.
explain: git pull — fetch the remote's commits and move this branch forward
--ff-only — refuse if a merge would be needed, so your history is never rewritten

variants.title: Fetch only
variants.description: Download the remote's commits without changing your files.
explain: git fetch --all — download new commits from every remote
--prune — forget remote branches that were deleted
your files and branches are not changed

actions.title: Push
actions.description: Send your commits on this branch to its remote.
explain: git push — upload your new commits to the remote
Asks first because other people may see them

actions.title: Stash changes
actions.description: Put your uncommitted changes aside, safely, to bring back later.
explain: git stash push — set the changes aside and clean the working folder
--include-untracked — include new files git hasn't seen yet
-m — a name so you can recognise it
Bring it back later with: git stash pop

variants.title: List stashes
variants.description: Show what's been set aside.
explain: git stash list — every stash, newest first
